text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU inference queue for cluster-prod-gpu has exceeded threshold. queue_length=2147, hpa_desired_replicas=0. Current replicas=6, max_replicas=6. Autoscaler status: no new scale events in last 12m.

Dave_oncall: on it. paging @jen_oncall and @mike_sre. seeing throttled responses in the logs?

Jen_oncall: I got the page. joining. quick check: is metrics adapter returning custom metrics? if adapter is lagging HPA won't scale.

Mike_sre: Checking Prometheus -> adapter -> metrics-server chain now. prometheus shows `gpu_queue_length` increasing for the last 30m. adapter scrape latency looks high.

Sara_prod: Customer reports rising 429s for long-running generation requests. ticket #INC-4123 has initial complain — they say recent spikes around 18:05 UTC.

Ellen_support: i've acknowledged on the ticket and added context that we're investigating autoscaling. will update customers every 15m.

Dave_oncall: runbook step 1: validate custom metric. Mike, can you curl the adapter metrics endpoint?

Mike_sre: curl output shows 504 from the adapter proxy intermittently. command: `curl -sS http://metrics-adapter.prod:8000/metrics | head` returns nothing sometimes. Logs show `timeout while reading from upstream`.

Mike_sre: Adapter pod list:
```
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=custom-metrics-adapter
NAME                                            READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
custom-metrics-adapter-0                        0/1     Running   4          2d
custom-metrics-adapter-1                        1/1     Running   0          2d
```

Ops-bob: looks like one replica is flapping and the adapter is served by a headless svc so load can be uneven. Why is HPA_desired_replicas=0 in the alert? maybe metrics API returning empty?

Dave_oncall: check `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 | jq '.'` and also `kubectl describe hpa gpu-inference-hpa -n prod`

Mike_sre: describe HPA shows:
```
Name:                          gpu-inference-hpa
Namespace:                     prod
Metrics:                       ( current / target )
  gpu-queue-length              N/A / 1000 requests
Events:                        failed to get metrics from custom metrics API: internal server error
```

Jen_oncall: confirms HPA failing to read metrics. Next step: check adapter logs for 5xx errors and restart the faulty pod. I'll tail logs now.

Jen_oncall: logs from adapter-0: `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address` then restart loop. adapter-1 healthy but under pressure. Restarting adapter-0 to get it out of crashloop.

Deploy-bot: :package: Deployment custom-metrics-adapter rolling restart triggered by jen_oncall.

Dave_oncall: While adapter restarts, we should mitigate customer impact: manual scale. kubectl scale deployment gpu-worker --replicas=12 -n prod. This will temporarily increase capacity until HPA recovers.

Mike_sre: issuing manual scale now. command: `kubectl scale deploy/gpu-worker -n prod --replicas=12` -> returned ok.

Sara_prod: on ticket: telling customer we are performing emergency scaling and investigating root cause. ETA update in 15m.

Ellen_support: customer notes some requests still queueing; they asked about SLA credit. I've escalated to TAM.

Dave_oncall: monitor queue after scaling. Mike, what does prometheus show for queue_length per-worker?

Mike_sre: after scale, queue_length per replica dropped ~40% but overall queue still at ~1200 and falling slowly. We saw a flurry of backlog hits from long-running inferences (seq len ~4096). Batching settings at the runtime increased per-token latency.

Ops-bob: runtime logs show KV cache miss storms — likely caused by many different model variants being requested concurrently. That's increasing compute time per request.

Jen_oncall: adapter ready now, `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` returns metrics. HPA now shows non-N/A metrics.

Dave_oncall: great. can HPA scale back automatically now? verify HPA target calculation.

Mike_sre: HPA has picked up the metric and is computing desired replicas=14 (based on queue metric). but cluster max_replicas is 14 and nodepool autoscaling is at quota. We're currently at 12 (manual). If HPA requests extra nodes, cloud autoscaler is being rate-limited.

Jen_oncall: cloud autoscaler logs show API rate limit errors from cloud provider while requesting new GPU nodes. filing cloud request ticket but that's slower. For live mitigation, keep manual replica increase to 14 and consider temporary offload to Dedicated pool.

Dave_oncall: Can we route lower-priority traffic to a fallback model (cpu nodes) to free GPU capacity? Sara, what's the percentage of traffic that can be degraded without major customer impact?

Sara_prod: approx 20% of non-paying sandbox traffic ok to degrade. For paying customers, only best-effort. We should move sandbox to a CPU fallback. I'll coordinate feature-flag flip.

Ellen_support: updated paying-cust to say degraded but active; sandbox moved to fallback now.

Mike_sre: implementing a temporary routing rule to direct sandbox route -> cpu-fallback pool. Patch: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: routing-overrides
  namespace: infra
data:
  sandbox_route: "cpu-pool"
EOF`

Deploy-bot: :rocket: Routing config applied. verifying traffic shift.

Mike_sre: sandbox traffic dropped from GPU pool by 95%. queue decreased to ~400 and trending down. Good.

Dave_oncall: status check: adapter stable, HPA reading metrics, manual replicas=14, cloud nodes pending. Customer impacts: 429 spikes reduced to intermittent, Majority of paying traffic served. Let's do on-call handoff in 20m once stable.

Jen_oncall: I'll take the next shift at 19:00 UTC. handing off to jen_oncall. Notes: root cause likely a combination of (1) custom-metrics-adapter crash reducing visibility to HPA, (2) cloud node quota/rate limits preventing autoscaler from fulfilling HPA desired nodes, (3) workload variability (cache misses) spiking GPU time.

Dave_oncall: ack. I'll stay available for escalation. Mike, please capture logs and exact timestamps for postmortem. Ellen, continue customer comms. Sara, follow up on routing and potential feature-flag reversion timeline.

Mike_sre: collecting logs now. saving adapters logs, HPA events, kube-scheduler events and cloud_autoscaler events. command snippets saved:
```
kubectl logs -n kube-system custom-metrics-adapter-0 --previous > /tmp/adapter-0.log
kubectl get hpa -n prod gpu-inference-hpa -o yaml > /tmp/hpa.yaml
gcloud compute operations list --filter="gpu-nodepool" > /tmp/cloud-ops.log
```

Ops-bob: quick mitigation suggestion for the future: consider adding a secondary metrics adapter replica in a different AZ and implement readiness probe to avoid head-of-service failover to flapping pods. Also add circuit-breaker in HPA evaluation to avoid desired=0 if metrics API returns empty.

Jen_oncall: noted for postmortem. tagging owners: @mike_sre (metrics), @ops-bob (adapter infra), @sara_prod (routing & product communication), @dave_oncall (runbook).

Ellen_support: customers updated. one paying customer requested a postmortem; I've assigned CS owner.

Dave_oncall: marking incident as RESOLVED in 40m if no regression. summary for incident timeline for postmortem:
- 18:01 UTC: alert triggered - GPU queue > 2000 and HPA desired=0
- 18:03 UTC: oncall paged, initial triage - HPA failing to read custom metrics
- 18:10 UTC: identified custom-metrics-adapter pod crashloop; restarted/replaced faulty pod
- 18:14 UTC: manual scale gpu-worker -> 12 to alleviate backlog
- 18:25 UTC: routing change to offload sandbox traffic to cpu-pool
- 18:30 UTC: HPA regained metrics; desired replicas = 14, manual replicas adjusted to 14
- 18:45 UTC: queue reduced to acceptable levels (~200) and 429 spikes subsided
- 19:00 UTC: handoff to jen_oncall for monitoring and postmortem prep

Jen_oncall: will open incident report ticket and schedule postmortem meeting. adding timeline and owners.

Dave_oncall: thanks everyone. reactions: :thumbsup: :100:

infra-bot: Incident updated to state=mitigated by user=jen_oncall.

jen_oncall: I'm now the owner. if anything flares i'll @page the oncall rotation. otherwise i'll draft postmortem and propose follow-ups: replicate adapter across az, cloud quota review, improve HPA handling when custom metrics API returns empty, autoscaler retry/backoff tuning, investigate caching/serving to reduce variance.

ellen_support: I'll follow up customer with an ETA for the postmortem and the actions list.

Mike_sre: saving all artifacts to /incidents/1894529876/artifacts/ and will attach logs to the postmortem doc.

Dave_oncall: handing off. long day. good job triaging quickly.

jen_oncall: closing thread for now, will keep it updated in the postmortem doc. :lock:
